discrepancies.title: OM occupancy 98.0% vs rent roll 91.7%

sources.label: rent roll: 77 of 84 units let at 2026-10-31

discrepancies.why: The rent roll is unit-level and dated 2026-10-31; the OM figure (undated) is a headline the screen cannot trace to units. A gap of 6.3 points is about 5 units.

impact.basis: 5 units x average in-place rent AED 64,344: income the OM implies but the roll does not show (estimate)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date; reconcile the OM figure to unit numbers.

discrepancies.title: Cover says "fully tenanted" but the OM's own occupancy figure is 98%
discrepancies.why: The OM contradicts itself. The cover says fully tenanted and the highlights page says 98% occupied. Code has already found the rent roll shows 91.7% (77 of 84 units let, 7 vacant, plus 2 under renewal and 2 with notice served). The "fully tenanted" label is a broker claim and the rent roll does not support it. It overstates the stability of the income.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker which occupancy figure is right and for a dated, unit-by-unit occupancy statement. Underwrite on the rent roll (7 vacant units, 2 notices served, 2 under renewal), not on the cover claim.

discrepancies.title: Unit-mix average rents imply more income than the headline rent
discrepancies.why: Multiplying units by the average rents on page 4 gives about AED 5.43m a year for all 84 units. That is 21 x 40,800 + 42 x 64,171 + 21 x 89,474. It is well above the AED 4.95m headline. The table appears to show full-building rents, including vacant units, next to a headline income that only roughly matches the contracted rent of let units. The OM does not say which basis either figure uses. The rent roll shows potential rent of about AED 5.54m against in-place rent of about AED 4.95m.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the broker to reconcile the average-rent table to the AED 4.95m headline and to say whether the table uses asking or contracted rents. Rely only on contracted rents from the Ejari-backed rent roll.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Decline**: Fennel Court is in Dubai Sports City, which is outside the mandate's permitted areas (JVC, Dubai Silicon Oasis, International City, Al Barsha South, Business Bay). The deal fails on that hard filter, so we stop here. The other hard filters (asset type, freehold single title, unit count, price, building age, no related-party master lease) pass.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Fennel Court, Dubai Sports City, built in 2015 [[deal.completion_year]], with 84 units [[om.unit_count]].
- **Price:** asking AED 61.0m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The OM quotes AED 740 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]], on BUA.
- **Income:** direct leases with no master tenant. The rent roll shows in-place rent of AED 5.0m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]], with 77 units let [[rr.let_units]] and 7 vacant [[rr.vacant_units]]. That is 92% occupancy by units [[rr.occupancy_by_units]].

## Returns
For reference only; not decisive. The building sits outside the market reference areas, so it was not underwritten. There are no returns to show, and the soft mandate tests on returns, occupancy and expiries are recorded as unknown.

The OM's headline yield is 8.1% [[om.yield_stated]] on the asking price. The OM does not say whether that yield is gross or net. It also states no net income or operating costs. The operating statement shows NOI of AED 3.3m [[opex.noi_aed]] before any adjustments. We have not restated the OM yield on a buyer's basis.

## What would make it fail
It has already failed on location. Occupancy is also lower than the OM says (see below).

## Discrepancies
**OM occupancy against the rent roll (high severity).** The OM states 98% [[om.occupancy_stated]]. The rent roll, dated 31 October 2026 [[rr.as_of]], shows 91.7% [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.title]]. The screen relied on the rent roll because it is unit-level. The OM figure is undated and cannot be traced to units. The gap of 6.3 points [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.why]] is about 5 units [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.why]]. That is roughly AED 322k [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.impact_aed]] of income the OM implies and the roll does not show (estimate).

A lower-severity item, on the OM's unit-mix average rents, is not discussed here.

## Checks before diligence
Only worth doing if the committee reconsiders the mandate.
- Get the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date. Reconcile the OM occupancy to unit numbers.
- Tenants' security deposits of AED 240,100 [[notice.security_deposits]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold, single title, buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate from Dubai Municipality.
- Affection plan and permitted use: residential use and permitted floors match the building.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence completion and fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
- Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.

## Assumptions
No underwriting assumptions were applied. The deal was declined on the mandate before any exit yield, rent path, vacancy or leverage view was used. The figures above come from the OM, the rent roll and the operating statement as presented.
